stem_book: From the following data of ΔH of the following reactions, C(s) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g); ΔH = −110 kJ and C(s) + H₂O(g) → CO(g) + H₂(g); ΔH = 132 kJ, calculate the mole composition of the mixture of steam and oxygen on being passed over coke at 1273 K, keeping temperature constant (i.e. the heat evolved by the first reaction exactly balances the heat absorbed by the second). Give the mole ratio n(O₂)/n(H₂O).
reason: Print has 'stream' for 'steam'; 'mole composition' could be a ratio or mole fractions — fixed the answer form as n(O₂)/n(H₂O) to match the key 0.6/1
work: 1 mol O₂ burns 2 C → 2×110 = 220 kJ released; y mol H₂O absorbs 132y: 220x = 132y → x/y = 0.6
